title: Certificates of Deposit: Early Withdrawal Penalty Calculation and Payout of Proceeds
content:
When a withdrawal from the bank's Certificates of Deposit is classified as an early full or early partial withdrawal, a penalty is charged. This page defines the size of that penalty, what the owner receives, and how the proceeds may be paid.

## Size of the penalty

The penalty is a number of days of simple interest on the principal the request removes. It is the penalty basis, multiplied by the penalty rate, multiplied by the penalty days, divided by the tier's days in the year, with the outcome rounded half-up to the cent.

- **Penalty basis.** For a partial withdrawal, the sum requested. For a full withdrawal, the whole principal balance after any accrued interest has been credited on the day of withdrawal.
- **Penalty days.** The tier's standard penalty days. On principal withdrawn within six calendar days after funding, the penalty days are instead the greater of the tier's standard penalty days and the six-day minimum, on every tier.
- **Penalty rate.** Each tier names the certificate's interest rate as the rate on which a penalty rests. The original wording that multiplied by the interest rate figure recorded on the certificate, divided by 100, is **no longer in force**; it has been replaced by the rate the bank's current terms fix for the term.

The penalty is taken out of principal even where it is larger than the interest the certificate has earned.

## Tier settings

| Tier | Standard penalty days | Minimum penalty days within six days of funding | Rate a penalty rests on | Penalty may cut into principal | Ways proceeds may be paid |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 90 | 7 | the certificate's interest rate | Yes | checking, savings, official check |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 0 | 7 | the certificate's interest rate | Yes | checking, savings, official check |
| 12-Month Certificate | 90 | 7 | the certificate's interest rate | Yes | checking, savings, official check |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 180 | 7 | the certificate's interest rate | Yes | checking, savings, official check |
| 36-Month Certificate | 180 | 7 | the certificate's interest rate | Yes | checking, savings, official check |
| 60-Month Certificate | 365 | 7 | the certificate's interest rate | Yes | checking, savings, official check |

## What the owner receives

- **Full withdrawal:** the owner receives what remains of the principal balance once the penalty is taken off it, and the certificate is closed.
- **Partial withdrawal:** the owner is paid the sum requested, and the penalty is taken from the principal that remains.

Proceeds are paid to a checking or savings account belonging to the same customer, or by official check.

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures; the penalty rate is assumed to be 4.00 percent and the year 365 days)

1. Full withdrawal from a 36-Month Certificate in its second year; principal after crediting accrued interest USD 20000.00. Penalty: 20000.00 multiplied by 4.00, divided by 100, multiplied by 180, divided by 365, that is 394.5205, rounded to USD 394.52. The owner receives USD 19605.48 and the certificate closes.
2. Partial withdrawal of USD 5000.00 from a 12-Month Certificate a month after funding. Penalty: 5000.00 multiplied by 4.00, divided by 100, multiplied by 90, divided by 365, that is 49.3151, rounded to USD 49.32. The owner receives USD 5000.00; USD 49.32 comes off the remaining principal.
3. Full withdrawal from an 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate three days after funding, principal USD 10000.00, assumed rate 3.50 percent. Penalty days are the greater of 0 and 7, so 7: 10000.00 multiplied by 3.50, divided by 100, multiplied by 7, divided by 365, that is 6.7123, rounded to USD 6.71.
